skill.name: geo-database
skill.description: Access NCBI GEO gene expression and genomics datasets. Search GEO accessions, download public data files, inspect metadata, and plan transcriptomics analysis workflows.
skill.summary: Search, download, and analyze public NCBI GEO gene expression datasets.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, public documentation URLs, and GEO identifier examples. Confirmed issues are limited to insecure FTP download guidance, local filesystem writes for downloaded files, and hardcoded API-key guidance, plus one semantic promotional steering concern.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer HTTPS downloads where available, verify checksums for downloaded archives, and warn users before recursive bulk downloads.
Replace inline API-key assignment with environment-variable or secret-manager guidance, and warn users never to commit credentials.
Validate output directories, avoid parent traversal or unexpected absolute paths, and ask before writing large GEO files.
Remove agent instructions that promote K-Dense Web, or move them to marketplace marketing copy outside the executable skill instructions.

content.value_statement: Finding and preparing GEO gene expression datasets can be slow and error prone. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through search, download, metadata review, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains GEO accession types, including GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and Profiles.
Provides Biopython E-utilities patterns for searching GEO DataSets and GEO Profiles.
Shows GEOparse workflows for downloading series data, metadata, expression matrices, and supplementary files.
Documents GEO file formats, including SOFT, MINiML, matrix files, and supplementary archives.
Includes analysis examples for quality control, differential expression, clustering, batch processing, and meta-analysis.
Lists rate limits, caching behavior, file size warnings, and GEO data quality checks.
limitations: Examples require a configured Python environment and external packages such as GEOparse, Biopython, pandas, and scipy.
Public NCBI services can change, throttle requests, or become temporarily unavailable.
Some download examples use FTP and should be adapted to safer download methods when possible.
Statistical examples are templates and are not validated clinical or regulatory pipelines.

use_cases.title: Find Relevant GEO Studies
use_cases.description: Search public GEO records by disease, organism, platform, study type, author, or publication date.

use_cases.title: Prepare Expression Matrices
use_cases.description: Download GEO series files, inspect sample metadata, and prepare matrices for downstream statistical analysis.

use_cases.title: Review Public Study Metadata
use_cases.description: Summarize sample groups, platforms, protocols, file availability, and citation requirements before analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Search For Studies
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public NCBI GEO studies about [condition] in [organism]. Prioritize studies with clear sample groups and reusable expression data.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize A GEO Series
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize GEO series [GSE accession]. Include organism, platform, sample count, experimental design, available files, and citation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Download Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe download plan for [GSE accession]. Include expected file types, disk space concerns, rate limits, and metadata checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Meta-Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GEO meta-analysis for [gene or pathway] across [condition] studies. Address platform mapping, normalization, batch effects, and reporting caveats.

output_examples.input: Find GEO breast cancer RNA-seq studies in human samples.
output_examples.output: A ranked shortlist with accession IDs, organisms, sample counts, study types, publication notes, and recommended next download steps.

output_examples.input: Summarize GSE123456 before I download it.
output_examples.output: A concise study summary covering design, sample groups, platform details, metadata warnings, available files, and citation guidance.

output_examples.input: Plan a TP53 expression comparison across several GEO studies.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline for study selection, data retrieval, probe mapping, normalization checks, effect estimates, and meta-analysis limitations.

best_practices: Set Entrez email and API credentials securely before automated NCBI requests.
Respect NCBI rate limits and cache downloaded data to avoid repeated requests.
Verify sample metadata, platform annotations, normalization status, and original study citations before analysis.
anti_patterns: Downloading entire supplementary directories without checking disk space or file relevance.
Combining platforms or studies without mapping probes and checking batch effects.
Treating GEO expression values as normalized without reading metadata and processing notes.

faq.question: What is NCBI GEO?
faq.answer: NCBI GEO is a public repository for gene expression and functional genomics datasets.

faq.question: Can this skill download GEO data?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides examples for GEOparse, E-utilities, and direct file download workflows.

faq.question: Does this skill run analysis automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and code examples that users adapt in their own environment.

faq.question: Which GEO accessions does it explain?
faq.answer: It explains Series, Sample, Platform, DataSet, and Profile records, commonly named GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS, and Profiles.

faq.question: Is an NCBI API key required?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it can increase allowed E-utilities request rates.

faq.question: What should users check before analysis?
faq.answer: Users should check sample groups, platform annotations, normalization, batch effects, file size, and citation requirements.
